errors.description: The deep 9.0 cm hem allowance leaves no readable outward cue, so the hem depth cannot be judged from the photograph.
errors.expected: Per the drawing, the top of the inside hem allowance sits a little under one third of the leg width above the bottom edge, hinted at by the extra weight and a barely perceptible pressed line.
errors.actual: The leg reads as one uniform surface down to the bottom edge; no pressed line or change in body marks where the allowance ends inside.
errors.correction: This is inherent to the option: on a plain hem the allowance is interior, and the drawing's red line is annotation that must NOT be rendered as an outside line. If regenerated, push only for a marginally heavier, denser fall of cloth in the bottom third of the leg - never a visible line, band or fold, which would read as a cuff and be a Critical error.

errors.description: The frame reaches roughly one and a half shoe-lengths above the hem rather than the intended one shoe-length, so the top third of the frame is featureless leg.
errors.expected: Top edge of frame at mid-calf, about one shoe-length above the bottom edge of the trouser leg.
errors.actual: Top edge sits near knee height; the hem and shoe occupy the lower third of the frame.
errors.correction: Lower the top frame edge to mid-calf while keeping the full leg width, the whole shoe and a sliver of floor inside the frame; do not move the camera in laterally.

notes: Attempt 1. The critical failure mode for this option - substituting a turn-up / cuff for a plain hem - was avoided cleanly: the outer leg is one continuous surface falling to a single pressed bottom edge, with no band, fold, ridge or outside stitching. Orientation is a true side-left view, the full leg width and whole shoe are in frame with a floor sliver, and no red or annotation leaked in from the drawing. The one unavoidable limitation is that a 9.0 cm plain hem allowance lives entirely inside the leg, so its depth is not photographically verifiable from the outside; the drawing conveys it only via a red position marker, which the annotation rule forbids rendering. Depth is therefore recorded as a Minor rather than driving a regeneration, because any attempt to make the allowance line visible on the outside would read as a cuff - the exact Critical error this option must avoid.
